text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- About 16,000 families benefit from range of programmes introduced by Housing Board since 1994 to help low-income households buy own flats.
- Next challenge for Education Ministry to retain newly-recruited teachers, says Minister for Education Teo Chee Hean at promotion exercise for more than 700 education officers.
- Fifty-seven-year-old man charged in court with practising medicine without registration.
- Sixteen-year-old boy sentenced to 15 years in jail and 24 strokes of the cane for drug trafficking and consumption.
- Mainboard-listed Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp, which has announced plans to branch into health-care business in region, may be aspiring to become next Raffles Medical Group, sources say.

- Malaysian dollar strengthens and interest rates ease as market reacts to Bank Negara decision to control ringgit swap sales to offshore groups in bid to curb excessive speculation against local currency.
- Basic telephone bidders will seek clarification from Telecommunication Authority of Singapore Friday on regulator's recent decision to introduce more licences by 2002.

- In an unusual move, U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch succeeds in getting Singapore High Court to order former financial consultant Kevin Wallace to come to Singapore to be cross-examined on list of assets he provided to court here.

- Malaysian ringgit opens more than two percent stronger in knee-jerk reaction to weekend measures to curb speculation, but closes at M$2.6120 to U.S. dollar for net gain of just 0.9 percent against last Friday.
- Cockpit Hotel owner, Teo Lay Swee, is latest entrant to UK hotel market with purchase of Paragon Hotel in London from Arab group.
- Businessman Mirzan Mahathir expected to seal deal to buy big chunk of national shipping company Malaysia International Shipping Corp for about 2 billion ringgit soon.
- Despite 17 percent drop in turnover, Indonesian-linked United Pulp & Paper achieves 89 percent surge in after-tax profit to Singapore $1.72 million for half year ended June 30.
- Amcol Holdings' key Japanese partner Tetsuro Funai did not wish to deal with new batch of shareholders led by Indonesian Henry Pribadi, it was revealed during insider trading trial.

- Diversified construction group Wee Poh Holdings says subsidiaries Wee Poh Construction and W & P Piling clinch contracts totalling S$32.4 million in value; associate company, OVM Prestress, has also secured job worth about S$460,000.
- DBS Bank plans to sell more securities backed by corporate bonds, following successful sale of such securities linked to Teledata bonds.
